title: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks companion spec
description:
Define a new JMAP Chat Tasks companion spec (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00) binding JMAP Tasks (draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06) TaskLists to Spaces.

The original near-term portion of this epic (registering urn:jmap:chat:cap:task under Endpoint.type and MessageAction.type) is already present in the main draft (line 226 of draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md, since the initial scaffolding commit 20a7b81). MessageAction.type :252 explicitly inherits the Endpoint type URI namespace. No further work needed at the URN-registration level.

OUTSTANDING WORK (companion-spec design)

Four design topics, each with open sub-decisions that need direction before a sub-bead can be filed:

1. TaskList ↔ Space binding
- One TaskList per Space (cleanest model)? Multiple TaskLists per Space (one for tracked work, one for ad-hoc)? Zero or N optional?
- Field on Space (e.g., spaceTaskListId) vs. new SpaceTaskList object connecting them?
- Lifecycle: TaskList created on Space create automatically? On first task-related action? Manually?
- Cascade: when a Space is destroyed, what happens to its bound TaskList(s)? Inherit, orphan, or destroy?

2. Permission mapping
- Does a new manage_tasks permission join the closed Space-permission vocabulary, or are TaskList rights derived from existing permissions (manage_channels? send?)?
- How do TaskList ACLs (which exist independently in JMAP Tasks) interact with Space membership? Override, intersection, or merge?
- Read vs. write granularity on Tasks: who can mark complete, reassign, add subtasks?

3. Task ↔ Chat back-reference
- A chatId field on Task pointing to a discussion thread Chat. What kind of Chat — channel (subject to Space permission model), group (member-list-driven), or a special new kind?
- Cardinality: can a Task have multiple threads? One canonical, others auxiliary?
- Lifecycle: when a Task closes, what happens to the Chat? Archive, leave open, destroy?
- Discoverability: does the Chat advertise its bound Task via a chat-level taskId field?

4. urn:jmap:chat:cap:task MessageAction URI format
- Concrete URI shape: urn:jmap:chat:cap:task:<taskListId>:<taskId>? Or http(s)-style JMAP Tasks URLs?
- Parser rules; how a client extracts taskListId and taskId from the URI
- UX: does the MessageAction render as just a link, or with embedded task preview (title, status, due date)?

Decomposes naturally into one design-decision bead (g71.1, like fig9.1) followed by one or more implementation beads once the decisions land. Implementation may also gate on draft-ietf-jmap-tasks reaching a stable enough version to depend on.

P4: not urgent. The URN-registration work that would have been the near-term win is already done; what remains is substantial design and probably waits on appetite and on the JMAP Tasks upstream draft.
notes: Aspirational placeholder. Near-term action (adding urn:jmap:chat:cap:task to well-known MessageAction and Endpoint types) is already covered by jmap-chat-spec-owe. Full companion spec is speculative — only pursue if there is a concrete deployment need for Space-bound TaskLists.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 8453a59 (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-tasks-00.md, 330 lines) plus cross-reference updates in 219b9ee. Design decisions made autonomously per Mark's direction: be inspired by fielded systems (Slack Lists, Microsoft Teams + Planner, Linear/Jira chat bridges) but do not over-constrain; use the c93e545/38055ec impl-defined latitude pattern for permission policy.
